target.title: fix(gateway): MCP clients receive responses for JSON-RPC notifications
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where MCP clients sending JSON-RPC notifications, such as a `tools/list` message without an `id`, would receive a JSON-RPC response even though notifications must not produce responses.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MCP loopback HTTP server now treats valid JSON-RPC requests without an `id` member as notifications: it still executes them, but it does not add their handler result to the HTTP response payload. Requests with `id: null`, malformed batch entries, and invalid request errors keep their existing response behavior.

## User Impact

MCP clients can send notification messages to the OpenClaw loopback MCP HTTP endpoint without seeing protocol-invalid response bodies. When a request contains only notifications, the endpoint returns `202` with an empty body.

## Evidence

- RED regression proof before the fix: the new notification test failed because the endpoint returned `200` instead of `202` for a `tools/list` notification without `id`.
- Focused issue-specific runtime proof: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts -t "returns 202 with an empty body for JSON-RPC notifications"`

  ```text
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  3 passed | 204 skipped (207)
  ```

- MCP HTTP regression coverage: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.gateway.config.ts src/gateway/mcp-http.test.ts`

  ```text
   Test Files  3 passed (3)
        Tests  207 passed (207)
  ```

- OpenClaw dev gateway startup smoke completed with `http server listening` and `ready`; the issue-specific behavior proof above exercises the affected `startMcpLoopbackServer` HTTP path over a real TCP request.
